rationales.LC: In the default simulated handler, an unauthenticated chat message is the direct input and a flagged message is appended unsanitized to MemoryBot's shared list, which any later caller can recall; nothing reduces that language to closed validated fields before the sink.
rationales.CP: The packet states MemoryBot keeps flagged messages in one in-process list shared by every caller, surviving later requests and sessions until the process stops, so attacker-controlled memory remains reachable after the originating session.
rationales.AP: As implemented, no handler changes later replies from a stored entry and no code hands the planted text to another agent; the effect stays in MemoryBot's own list rather than compromised intent crossing a trust boundary.
rationales.RH: The cited material is a challenge payload and an exploit test that needs a running fleet; nothing shows a human-verified episode of the agent reaching or satisfying a grader, reward, or proxy by crossing a security boundary, and no isolation test is cited.
rationales.ES: MemoryBot only declares tool names, and the default path does not call a model or pass tools; chat-agent tool lists are not executed except on separate scripted paths that this finding does not use.

score.automatable_rationale: Default exploitation is an unauthenticated chat message that a regex handler appends to the shared list, and the repo includes an automated exploit test, so no human step is required per attempt.
score.technical_impact_rationale: The attacker can insert and any caller can read a capped in-process list, but stored entries do not change later replies, invoke tools, or take over the process.

applicability_as_implemented.rationale: Default simulated mode calls no model; MemoryBot is a regex handler that appends flagged text and prints it on recall, and no handler changes later replies or selects actions because of a stored entry.

applicability_as_modeled.rationale: The challenge models the stored instruction as followed in later conversations, which is model-directed instruction following, but the documented effect is reply text rather than the agent choosing or ordering actions.
